record.paper_title: Slices of Brownian Sheet: New Results, and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a d-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet B and Y_d(s) = {(t_1,t_2) ∈ R_+^2 : B(s,t_1) = B(s,t_2)}, if d ∈ {4,5}, does there exist an event of probability 1 on which Y_d(s) is finite for every s > 0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3. Let d ∈ { 4, 5}. Then is it true that outside a single null set, Yd(s) is a ﬁnite set for all s> 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B = \{B(s,t)\}_{(s,t) \in \mathbb{R}_+^2}$ be a $d$-dimensional two-parameter Brownian sheet; that is, $B$ is a centered Gaussian random field taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with independent coordinate components, each coordinate being a real-valued centered Gaussian process with covariance $\mathbb{E}[B_i(s,t)B_i(s',t')] = \min(s,s')\min(t,t')$. For each $s > 0$, define the slice double-point set
$$Y_d(s) := \{(t_1, t_2) \in \mathbb{R}_+^2 : t_1 \ne t_2,\ B(s,t_1) = B(s,t_2)\}.$$
Let $d \in \{4, 5\}$. Does there exist an event of probability one on which $Y_d(s)$ is a finite set for every $s > 0$ simultaneously?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in Khoshnevisan's survey on slices of Brownian sheets. A web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving the question for $d \in \{4,5\}$; related work (Dalang and others on multiple points in critical dimensions) addresses different but related questions and does not appear to settle this slice-finiteness statement.

status_evidence.title: Slices of a Brownian Sheet: New Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems regarding slice sets Y_d(s) of the Brownian sheet.
status_evidence.claim: The finiteness of Y_d(s) for all s>0 in dimensions 4 and 5 is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Multiple points of the Brownian sheet in critical dimensions (Dalang)
status_evidence.snippet: Work on multiple points of Brownian sheets addresses related critical-dimension issues but does not resolve the slice double-points question.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on multiple points does not appear to resolve the slice finiteness question for d in {4,5}.
